Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-109618 affectant PHP.

CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog and updated the PHP Alert, Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching :   CVE-2026-109618 – PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability  CVE-2026-109619 – PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability  These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.  Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.  While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-111497 affectant Google.

Alarm bells ratcheted up yet again about an AI-discovered vulnerability that could — if exploited in the wild — destabilize vast stretches of the internet.  The critical defect — CVE-2026-111497 — affects the Google-developed Brotli decompression library that’s bundled into many components, applications and cloud services riding on open-source software. The buffer overflow vulnerability, which OpenAI Codex Security discovered and Node.js disclosed in a Oct. 21 security advisory , can trigger system crashes and remote code execution.  Researchers haven’t observed any active exploitation of the defect in real networks, but concerns are mounting. Multiple vendors and software packages, including Microsoft and Python, that rely on vulnerable versions of Brotli have rushed emergency patches out to address the risk of exploitation in their respective systems. Wiz researchers warned that “ 91% of cloud environments have resources vulnerable to CVE-2026-111497 and 82% of cloud environments have publicly exposed Node.js instances.” The attack surface is “extremely broad and vast, but much of the impact of exploitation depends entirely on its implementation and how it is used within that piece of software,” said Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at watchTowr. Paxton, who is locked in a close Senate race, has sued or settled with several tech companies in the last year, including Roblox, TikTok and Meta.

At the top of Friday’s lawsuit , Altman’s past proclamation that AI will “probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there’ll be great companies” is featured prominently in italics.

A spokesperson for OpenAI said the company “works closely with experts to continually improve ChatGPT, mitigate risks and build additional safeguards. Governments have an important role to play in setting robust safety standards for AI, and we’re committed to working with Texas and other states on advancing pragmatic AI policies that apply to the entire AI industry - not just one company."

Zheng Zhao and his co-conspirators allegedly deceived 174 U.S. residents into sending funds to a globally coordinated fake investment operation with ties to Cambodia.

Zheng Zhao was extradited from the Netherlands to the United States to face a conspiracy to commit money laundering charge that could keep him in prison for 20 years.

Prosecutors accuse Zhao and his co-conspirators of operating a global cryptocurrency investment scheme out of multiple countries, including scam centers in Cambodia.

The cybercrime ring allegedly reached out to U.S.-based victims proactively via social media, phone calls, text messages and online dating sites to establish a deceitful relationship and build trust. Eventually, Zhao and his co-conspirators promoted cryptocurrency investments to the victims and directed them to send funds through fake sites that resembled legitimate trading platforms.

Victims were told their investments were growing in value, yet they were already transferred from U.S. bank accounts controlled by the co-conspirators to an account at Deltec Bank in the Bahamas, officials said. The crew allegedly converted the victim funds to Tether before transferring the assets to a digital wallet controlled in Cambodia.

The stolen funds were ultimately distributed to leaders of scam networks throughout the region, officials said.

Eight of Zhao’s co-conspirators previously pleaded guilty participating in the investment scam conspiracy, including Shengsheng He and Jingliang Su , who were sentenced to 51 months and 46 months in prison, respectively.

Nick Anderson, acting director of CISA, wrote in the new CISA document: “The threat landscape we face today is not static. Nation-state actors and other malicious adversaries continue to grow more sophisticated in their efforts to compromise our networks, and there is no guarantee that a strong defense will eliminate intrusions.”

He added: “As President Trump has reminded us, resilience must be the foundation of our approach. We must ensure that when adversaries gain a foothold, we are prepared to detect them quickly, evict them decisively, and keep critical operations running without interruption.”

The strategy is designed to execute recent White House policy announcements around cybersecurity.

The Trump administration is breaking the law after being more than a month overdue on declassifying a court opinion on the surveillance of U.S. citizens, according to two senators and a coalition of civil liberties groups. Release of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) opinion has been closely tied to reauthorizing Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), which lapsed this summer, although collection authority has continued under another court ruling that runs through March of next year. Under Section 702, the government can warrantlessly search foreign targets’ electronic and phone communications using the personal information of Americans who have been in contact with them. In the FISC opinion that the administration has not declassified, a judge objected to tools the government has created to let analysts process messages.
